text: dsh-context-handoff 是面向 DSH Web 的会话上下文交接插件，通过 /handoff 命令和右侧边栏面板，把长会话整理成可供新会话继续工作的 Markdown 文件。它会根据 token 用量比较继续当前会话与切换新会话的相对成本，支持手动生成交接、查看计划和状态、管理每工作区自动模式，并可在空闲会话达到阈值后先压缩再交接。摘要优先使用当前配置的模型，失败时可生成确定性摘要；交接文件默认写入工作区 .dsh/handoff。摘要请求会把会话内容发送给配置的模型服务。

dsh-context-handoff turns long DSH Web sessions into Markdown handoff files. Use /handoff to write one or /handoff plan to compare token costs. The sidebar shows context and auto mode; idle sessions can be handed off at a threshold. Summaries use the configured model or a deterministic fallback.
想把很长的 DSH 会话整理成新会话能接着用的交接文档。
DSH 能不能估算继续聊和另开会话哪个更省 token？
Create a concise handoff from my long session so I can resume the work in a fresh session.
dsh-context-handoff 的功能「手动生成会话交接」：通过 /handoff 命令生成总结，并将交接内容写成 Markdown 文件，供新会话读取继续工作。
dsh-context-handoff 的功能「比较会话 token 成本」：使用 /handoff plan 查看继续当前会话或生成交接并切换的预估 token 成本、盈亏点和建议时机；计算使用 token 数量而非货币账单。
dsh-context-handoff 使用当前会话配置的模型生成摘要，会把会话消息发送给该模型服务；代码未固定具体服务商，取决于 DSH 的模型路由配置。

dsh-context-handoff README · dsh-context-handoff：> Token-aware context handoff for DeepSeek Harness (dsh): summarize a long session into a self-contained Markdown file, decide with measured token economics whether to continue or start fresh, and resume in a new session.

[中文](README.zh.md) · [Publishing](docs/PUBLISHING.md) · [Design](docs/DESIGN.md) · [GitHub](https://github.com/idianzi/dsh-context-handoff)

dsh-context-handoff README · dsh-context-handoff：- **`/handoff`** writes a handoff document that a fresh session can read directly.
- **`/handoff plan`** compares continuing with switching using `ctx.tokenMeter`; it makes no model call.
- **Sidebar switch** in the right sidebar panel turns auto mode on/off per workspace.
- **Auto mode** writes the handoff, creates a fresh session, and queues the resume prompt when an idle session crosses the threshold.
- **Deterministic fallback** still produces a conservative digest when the model is unavailable or fails.
- **Secret redaction** removes common API keys, tokens, and private keys before writing.
- **Local ledger** records each generation so `/handoff stats` can report cumulative summary cost and projected savings.

dsh-context-handoff README · Why not just compact?：dsh's `/compact` replaces older history with a summary **inside the same session**. It answers: "the context is nearly full, but I want to keep working here."

dsh-context-handoff README · Why not just compact?：This plugin answers a different question: **when is it worth leaving the session with a high-quality handoff?** Compaction keeps paying for its summary every turn; a handoff file is read once by a new session and the old 100k-token history is no longer re-sent. Writing too early wastes the summary cost and discards useful detail; writing too late has already paid for many oversized turns. The plugin computes where the break-even point is.

dsh-context-handoff README · Why not just compact?：The two are not exclusive. The plugin reuses `/compact` to condense first and only writes the handoff when the context is still over the threshold afterwards, so the cheap move happens before the expensive one.

dsh-context-handoff README · Install：The package is not on npm yet, so install it from the repository:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:idianzi/dsh-context-handoff
```

Desktop users should install from **Plugins**; the CLI form works after the Desktop profile is initialized and the app is fully quit:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:idianzi/dsh-context-handoff
```

dsh-context-handoff README · Install：Once it is published to npm (see [docs/PUBLISHING.md](docs/PUBLISHING.md)) and listed in the market, `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-context-handoff` works the same way.

Local development:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-context-handoff
```

Verify with `/handoff help`. The command requires the `dsh-commands` UI adapter; auto mode works without it.

dsh-context-handoff README · Usage：| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `/handoff` | Write a handoff and report the comparison. |
| `/handoff plan [turns]` | Analyze only; no model call, no file. `turns` is the horizon (default `horizonTurns`). |
| `/handoff now [tokens]` | Write now with an explicit digest budget (minimum 600). |
| `/handoff status` | Current pressure plus the latest file. |
| `/handoff list` | Newest files in the output directory. |
| `/handoff stats` | Aggregate the local JSONL ledger. |
| `/handoff auto [on\|off]` | Show or set the per-workspace auto switch. |
| `/handoff help` | Help. |

dsh-context-handoff README · Sidebar panel：Next to the session title there is a small chip — **上下文 545k**, or **自动总结 545k** while auto mode is on. Clicking it expands the right sidebar and opens the handoff panel, so you do not have to know where the sidebar is. You can also open it from the right sidebar's add menu: **上下文交接 / Context Handoff**.

dsh-context-handoff README · Sidebar panel：- **Condensation is automatic and has no switch.** At the recommendation point the plugin condenses once with the same backend `/compact` uses (`compactNow` from `dsh-compaction-basic`), replacing older history with a single summary: up to `maxCompactionsPerSession` times per session (default 3), and it stops early when a condense frees less than 10% of the context.
- That backend lives inside the session's preset group (`isolate: { compaction: true }`), so a host-plane plugin cannot reach `ctx.compaction`. The plugin therefore drives it through the official command — `ctx.commands.execute(agent, '/compact')` — whose handler runs inside that scope and calls the same backend. The panel's compaction row reports which route was used: `agent`, `context`, `command`, or `none`.
- **A handoff only runs when the context is still over the threshold after condensing.** That step is what the switch controls: off means condense only, on means write the file and start a new session.
- The switch controls the new-session step of auto mode. It is stored in `.dsh/handoff/auto.json` and survives restarts.

dsh-context-handoff README · Sidebar panel：Auto mode is per workspace and performs at most one automatic handoff per source session.

Example plan:

```text
Context: 118k / 128k (92%), 10.0k headroom
Composition: 11.0k fixed prefix + 107k messages
Digest: 3.0k tokens (budget 3.0k)
Per-turn saving: 57.2k tokens (cache factor 0.55) · break-even 1.2 turns

The file goes to `.dsh/handoff/` by default and starts with YAML frontmatter, a copy-paste resume line, and then the summary. The resume workflow is:

dsh-context-handoff README · Sidebar panel：1. `/handoff plan 10` to check the economics.
2. `/handoff` when you are ready to leave.
3. Open a fresh session and paste `Read @.dsh/handoff/<file>.md and continue from the "Next steps" section.`
4. Continue from that section; keep the old session as evidence if useful.

The output directory also contains `ledger.jsonl` (token numbers, model, file name, session id; no conversation text). Set `ledger: false` to disable it.

dsh-context-handoff README · Token model：Measured inputs:

- `P` current prompt pressure (`tokenMeter.measure(session).totalTokens`).
- `S` fixed prefix every session pays (system prompt + tool schemas).
- `D` the handoff file's own token count (`tokenMeter.estimateMessage`).
- `H` comparison horizon in turns (default 8).
- `a` cache factor: `(1 - hitRate) + hitRate × cacheReadWeight`.

```text
Continue H turns:      H × P × a
Handoff + H new turns: P × a + D + switchOverhead + H × (S + D) × a

dsh-context-handoff README · Token model：Break-even turns R* = (P × a + D + overhead) / ((P - S - D) × a)

The quality threshold matters: at 18k tokens in a 128k window, switching may already be cheaper, but it throws away context you still need. Defaults are 55%, a 256k absolute cap, and an 8k reserve:

| Window | Recommendation point |
|---|---|
| 32k | 17.6k |
| 64k | 35.2k |
| 128k | 70.4k |
| 200k | 110k |
| 1M | 256k (absolute cap) |

dsh-context-handoff README · Token model：Worked example: `P=118k`, `S=11k`, `D=3k`, `H=8`, 50% cache hit, weight 0.1 → `a=0.55`; continuing ≈ 519k effective tokens, switching ≈ 131k, saving ≈ 388k, break-even ≈ 1.2 turns. The recommendation point is 70.4k.

These are relative token costs, not a bill: dsh has no cross-provider price table. Cache assumptions are configurable, and the meter's fixed heuristic is an approximation (especially for CJK and JSON schema). Treat the result as a decision aid, not billing data.

A bundle install already inserts the row; use `- id: context-handoff` to override it. For a hand-composed profile without the bundle patch, insert it explicitly:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: context-handoff
      name: dsh-context-handoff
```

dsh-context-handoff README · Configuration：| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `outputDir` | `.dsh/handoff` | Output directory, relative to the workspace or absolute. |
| `targetDigestTokens` | `3000` | Digest token budget. |
| `minDigestTokens` | `700` | Lower bound for small contexts. |
| `maxDigestTokens` | `8000` | Absolute cap. |
| `digestRatio` | `0.03` | Budget as a share of current context, then clamped. |
| `recommendAtRatio` | `0.55` | Quality threshold as a window fraction. |
| `recommendMaxTokens` | `256000` | Absolute cap for the recommendation point; `0` disables it. |
| `horizonTurns` | `8` | Cost-comparison horizon; at least 2. |
| `cacheHitRatio` | `0.5` | Assumed cache hit share. |
| `cacheReadWeight` | `0.1` | Relative cache-read cost. |
| `switchOverheadTokens` | `1500` | Re-orientation cost of a new session. |
| `keepFiles` | `20` | Files kept per directory; `0` disables pruning. |
| `auto` | `false` | Default for workspaces without an `auto.json` override. |
| `autoNewSession` | `true` | Auto mode creates a new session and queues the resume prompt. |
| `autoMinGrowthTokens` | `8000` | Minimum growth between auto handoffs. |
| `autoCooldownMinutes` |

dsh-context-handoff README · Configuration：Auto mode writes only when the workspace switch is on, the agent is idle, the session is not a subagent, the plan is useful, the recommendation point is crossed, this source session has not already completed an automatic handoff, and no recent handoff exists. It runs through `agent.runMaintenance()`, never interrupts a live turn, then creates a new root session in the same workspace with the resume prompt queued. The file remains valid if session creation fails.

dsh-context-handoff README · Privacy：Handoff files contain conversation text, paths, commands, and errors. They are written into your workspace; add `.dsh/handoff/` to `.gitignore`. Redaction is best-effort, not a security boundary. The summary call sends the conversation prefix to the configured model provider, exactly like normal chat. Auto mode makes background model calls and files; confirm the cost is acceptable before enabling it.

dsh-context-handoff README · Compatibility：Verified against **DSH Desktop 0.2.1-rc.3** (`dsh --version`): bundle composition, config-schema import, plugin load, `/handoff` command registration, presence of the client bundle in the Web boot graph, and retrieval of the bundle from `/plugins` in a disposable Web profile. Sidebar tab/pane registration is covered by the client bundle test; command execution, model calls, auto-state, new-session creation, and ledger behavior are covered by `npm test` with stubbed services. Real summary quality and visual rendering still depend on your dsh build and model. The plugin targets 0.2.x APIs; re-run both checks after a host upgrade.

dsh-context-handoff README · Development：```sh

```

Modules: `config`, `economics`, `digest`, `summarize`, `files`, `format`, `index`. See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) for the replay-versus-transcript decision, tool-pairing safety, and known limits.
